answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust is propagated by a bounded-length random walk, so influence decays when transitions cross sparse boundaries. A sybil cluster therefore appears as a low-conductance external cut: its escape probability, constrained by cut capacity and min-cut transitivity bounds, limits the stationary mass it can capture. Even if dune, saffron, or zephyr identities collude, their aggregate voting weight remains bounded by boundary conductance rather than population.
